title: Faster Mixing of the Jerrum-Sinclair Chain
authors: Xiaoyu Chen (LIDS, MIT, Cambridge, MA.), Weiming Feng (The University of Hong Kong, China.), Zhe Ju (Nanjing University, China.), Tianshun Miao (Nanjing University, China.), Yitong Yin (Nanjing University, China.), Xinyuan Zhang (Nanjing University, China.)
abstract: We show that the Jerrum-Sinclair Markov chain on matchings mixes in time Õ(Δ^2 m) on any graph with n vertices, m edges, and maximum degree Δ, for any constant edge weight λ > 0. For general graphs with arbitrary, potentially unbounded Δ, this provides the first improvement over the classic Õ(Δ^2 m) mixing time bound of Jerrum and Sinclair (1989) and Sinclair (1992). To achieve this, we develop a general framework for analyzing mixing times, combining ideas from the classic canonical path method with the "local-to-global" approaches recently developed in high-dimensional expanders, introducing key innovations to both techniques.

Remark 9 (Canonical path and multicommodity ﬂow
as transport ﬂow). The classical canonical path method,
and more generally, multicommodity ﬂow [5], [34], can
be interpreted as constructing a transport ﬂow from µ to

corresponds to a transport ﬂow Γ from µ to µ, where
each path γ ∈ P is sampled with probability w(γ). Thus,
a random path γ ∼ Γ induces an independent coupling
with itself through its endpoints (s(γ), t(γ)).
